sections.md:
This brief covers Directive (EU) 2023/959 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023, which amends Directive 2003/87/EC (the EU ETS Directive) and Decision (EU) 2015/1814 (the Market Stability Reserve Decision). It is structured as a Regulatory Fact Document under the regulatory_fact_document format.

**Convention notes:** The directive amends but does not replace the consolidated ETS Directive. References to articles are to the *amended* Directive 2003/87/EC as it stands post-2023 revision, not to standalone articles of Directive 2023/959 itself. The consolidated text as of 5 June 2023 is the operative instrument. All FACT citations draw from the primary source (id: 13f9585a-1f19-4b07-a0f7-df65ae0f5712) and corroborating sources as identified below.

**Workspace relevance filter:** This directive is analyzed through the lens of a freight forwarding operation whose transport mode priority is air primary, road secondary, ocean tertiary, and whose cargo verticals include live events, fine art, luxury goods, film and TV, high-value automotive, and humanitarian. The directive's maritime provisions are the highest-relevance stream for ocean-mode operations. The ETS2 (buildings, road transport, and additional sectors) stream is relevant to road-mode operations and fuel surcharge exposure. The aviation stream affects air-mode cost structure. The workspace's supply chain roles — freight forwarder, importer, customs broker — each carry distinct exposure profiles analyzed below.

**Dates:** This document is current as of 27 May 2026. The directive entered into force on 5 June 2023. Source content was retrieved and grounded at generation time.

---

## Maritime Compliance Chain

FACT: The directive defines "shipping company" as "the shipowner or any other organisation or person, such as the manager or the bareboat charterer, that has assumed the responsibility for the operation of the ship from the shipowner and that, on assuming such responsibility, has agreed to take over all the duties and responsibilities imposed by the International Management Code for the Safe Operation of Ships and for Pollution Prevention." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(3)(d)(w) inserting definition into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in any capacity (freight forwarder, NVOCC, or otherwise), meets the definition of "shipping company" under this article in any transaction requires counsel review of each operational arrangement. A freight forwarder that does not operate or manage vessels does not on its face meet this definition, but any NVO or vessel-operating arrangement would require specific legal analysis.

FACT: Article 3gc provides that "when the ultimate responsibility for the purchase of the fuel, or the operation of the ship, or both, is assumed by an entity other than the shipping company pursuant to a contractual arrangement, the shipping company is entitled to reimbursement from that entity for the costs arising from the surrender of allowances." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3gc as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any contractual arrangements the workspace holds with shipping companies constitute "assuming responsibility for the operation of the ship" such that the shipping company could seek reimbursement from the workspace requires counsel review of specific contract terms.

Operational implication: For the workspace acting as a shipper or cargo owner (not vessel operator), the ETS cost flows from shipping company → freight rate or surcharge → workspace → client. The workspace's position is as a cost recipient and potential pass-through entity, not a direct compliance obligor.

## Aviation Compliance Chain

Aircraft operators are the compliance entities for aviation ETS. The workspace, as a freight forwarder purchasing cargo space, is exposed through rate structures. No direct surrender obligation attaches to freight forwarders in the aviation stream.

## ETS2 Road Transport Compliance Chain

FACT: The directive defines "regulated entity" for ETS2 purposes as "any natural or legal person, except for any final consumer of the fuels, that engages in the activity referred to in Annex III" — that activity being "Release for consumption of fuels which are used for combustion in the buildings, road transport and additional sectors." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3(ae) inserting definition into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The regulated entity categories are aligned with excise duty liability under Council Directive (EU) 2020/262, specifically: "(i) where the fuel passes through a tax warehouse as defined in Article 3, point (11), of Council Directive (EU) 2020/262, the authorised warehousekeeper…; (ii) if point (i) of this point is not applicable, any other person liable to pay the excise duty…; (iii) if points (i) and (ii) of this point are not applicable, any other person that has to be registered by the relevant competent authorities of the Member State for the purpose of being liable to pay the excise duty." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3(ae)(i)–(iii) inserting definition into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, as a freight forwarder, is or could become an ETS2 "regulated entity" under any of these categories in any Member State requires counsel review. The point of regulation is upstream (fuel distributors), and freight forwarders are not ordinarily fuel distributors, but arrangements in specific jurisdictions or specific operational models could create exposure.

Operational implication: For road freight operations (drayage to ports, cross-border road freight in Europe), ETS2 cost will be passed through by trucking operators into rates from 2028. The workspace should build ETS2 cost escalation into multi-year European road freight contracts.

---

## For the Workspace as Freight Forwarder (Cost Monitoring and Contract Infrastructure)

**Maritime ETS cost tracking system:**
- **What to build:** A per-shipment ETS cost attribution capability that maps ocean freight invoices to their ETS surcharge components, segregated by route type (intra-EU = 100%, mixed = 50%).
- **Gap from current baseline:** If the workspace currently does not separate ETS surcharges from base freight in its cost accounting, this gap means ETS cost cannot be accurately reported to clients or modeled for contract pricing.
- **Deadline:** Immediate — 2026 compliance year (100% surrender) is underway.
- **Scope:** All ocean freight on EU-port-touching routes across Americas, Europe, and Asia trade lanes.

**Contract clause review:**
- **What to build:** A standard ETS cost pass-through clause for client service agreements covering ocean freight, reviewed against applicable law in the governing jurisdiction.
- **Gap:** Absent an explicit clause, ETS cost increases that arise mid-contract are absorbed in margin.
- **Deadline:** Apply to all new contracts and renewal events. Retroactive clauses are subject to negotiation.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* Clause language should be reviewed by counsel familiar with the law of the contract's governing jurisdiction, including whether English law (common for shipping contracts) or EU Member State law applies.

**Aviation ETS monitoring:**
- **What to build:** Rate monitoring process that tracks air freight rate changes attributable to the complete removal of aviation free allocation from 2026, specifically on intra-EEA routes and routes involving EU hub airports.
- **Cargo vertical priority:** Air primary mode — live events, fine art, humanitarian, luxury goods, film and TV.
- **Deadline:** 2026 rate review cycle.

**ETS2 road freight modeling:**
- **What to build:** Forecast model for European road freight rate escalation attributable to ETS2 fuel cost pass-through from 2028 onward.
- **Deadline:** Build by end of 2026; apply to multi-year European road freight contracts from 2027.

**Carrier compliance verification protocol:**
- **What to build:** A due diligence step for ocean carrier selection confirming active ETS monitoring plan approval, no outstanding surrender failures, and no expulsion order status.
- **Rationale:** An expulsion-ordered carrier cannot call EU ports; the workspace's cargo would be disrupted. This risk is acute for live events and humanitarian cargo with hard delivery deadlines.

---

## Plain-Language Summary

FACT: Directive (EU) 2023/959 was adopted on "10 May 2023" and published in the Official Journal of the European Union on "16.5.2023" as OJ L 130/134. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: Article 5 states "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union," which places the entry-into-force date at **5 June 2023**. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 5, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

The directive is the primary instrument of the EU's "Fit for 55" package as it applies to the EU ETS. Its structural changes span three distinct systems:

1. **EU ETS (ETS1) — existing cap-and-trade for power, industry, aviation:** Tighter cap trajectory, maritime sector inclusion from 2024, CBAM interaction with free allocation, strengthened Market Stability Reserve.
2. **ETS2 — new cap-and-trade for buildings, road transport, and additional sectors:** Separate system, upstream point of regulation (fuel distributors, not end-users), operational from 2028 following a one-year postponement.
3. **Market Stability Reserve amendments:** Higher intake rates, revised invalidation threshold, new ETS2-specific reserve section.

FACT: The directive's stated objective is achieving "a reduction in the emissions of the sectors covered by the EU ETS of 62 % compared to 2005" by 2030. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, recital (39), EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

## Why It Applies to the Workspace

The workspace operates as a freight forwarder arranging ocean freight, air freight, and road freight on behalf of clients. Three channels of exposure exist:

**Channel 1 — Ocean freight cost pass-through:** The directive extends EU ETS allowance surrender obligations to shipping companies operating vessels of 5,000 GT and above. Ocean carriers serving trade lanes used by the workspace (Americas, Europe, Asia) are covered entities. Those carriers pass allowance costs through freight rates and surcharges to shippers, including freight forwarders and their clients.

**Channel 2 — Air freight cost exposure:** The directive tightens the aviation cap and phases out free allocation for aircraft operators by 2026. Airlines pass ETS allowance costs into fuel surcharges and freight rates on intra-EEA and mixed routes.

**Channel 3 — Road freight cost exposure (ETS2):** ETS2 covers fuel distributors supplying road transport fuel. Fuel cost increases flow into road freight rates, affecting drayage, line-haul, and last-mile costs for cargo verticals including live events, luxury goods, and high-value automotive.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in any transaction where it acts as importer of record or shipper of record, bears a direct ETS compliance obligation (rather than a cost passed through by a carrier) depends on the specific contractual and regulatory classification of its role in each transaction. This is a legal determination requiring counsel review.

---

## A. Maritime ETS — Scope of Coverage (Article 3ga)

FACT: The directive specifies the following coverage fractions for maritime ETS allowance surrender:
- "fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State"
- "fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State"
- "one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State"
- "one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships within a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State"

*Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3ga(1) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification — neighboring container transhipment ports:** FACT: The directive provides that the Commission shall "by 31 December 2023, by means of implementing acts establish a list of neighbouring container transhipment ports" and update it "by 31 December every two years thereafter." A port qualifies if "the share of transhipment of containers… exceeds 65 % of the total container traffic of that port during the most recent twelve-month period" AND "that port is located outside the Union but less than 300 nautical miles from a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State." The list "shall not include ports located in a third country for which that third country effectively applies measures equivalent to this Directive." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3ga(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Industry interpretation (Sustainable Ships): The Commission adopted an Implementing Regulation on 26 October 2023 identifying Tanger Med (Morocco) and East Port Said (Egypt) as 'neighbouring container transhipment ports'. This act is to be revised every two years. *Source: Sustainable Ships EU ETS Maritime page, undated (current). https://www.sustainable-ships.org/rules-regulations/eu-ets. This is an industry secondary source cited for operational context.

**Effect on workspace cargo verticals:** For containers routed through Tanger Med or East Port Said as transhipment hubs before entering EU ports, stops at those ports are excluded from voyage start/end calculations. This reduces ETS exposure for certain Asia-Europe container flows. For the workspace's live events and film/TV equipment cargo moving in full container loads on hub-and-spoke routes, this is a routing cost factor worth confirming with ocean carriers.

## B. Phase-In Schedule (Article 3gb)

FACT: "Shipping companies shall be liable to surrender allowances according to the following schedule:
(a) 40 % of verified emissions reported for 2024 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12;
(b) 70 % of verified emissions reported for 2025 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12;
(c) 100 % of verified emissions reported for 2026 and each year thereafter in accordance with Article 12."

**Qualification — cancellation during phase-in:** FACT: "Where fewer allowances are surrendered compared to the verified emissions from maritime transport for the years 2024 and 2025, once the difference between verified emissions and allowances surrendered has been established in respect of each year, an amount of allowances corresponding to that difference shall be cancelled rather than auctioned pursuant to Article 10." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3gb as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Operational implication: From 2026, 100% of verified emissions on covered routes are subject to allowance surrender. The cost step-up from 70% (2025) to 100% (2026) is material — a 43% increase in surrender obligation year-over-year — and this should be modeled into freight budget planning for the remainder of 2026.

## C. Surrender Deadline and Compliance Cycle

FACT: Article 12(3) of the amended directive states: "The Member States, administering Member States and administering authorities in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: … (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(21)(c) replacing Article 12(3) of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification — stationary installations deadline change:** The same article moved the stationary installation surrender deadline from 30 April to 30 September (Article 16(3) amendment). This affects industrial clients but not the workspace's core freight operations.

## D. Penalty Provisions (Article 16)

FACT: Article 16 paragraph 3 of the amended directive applies a penalty of €100 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent for which no allowance has been surrendered. Article 1(23)(c) of Directive 2023/959 inserts paragraph 3a: "The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(23)(c)–(d) amending Article 16 of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The FAQ confirms: "heavy fines are imposed" for non-compliance: "if a company emits 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ falling within the scope of the EU ETS Directive during a reporting period, that company needs to buy and surrender 10,000 allowances by 30 September of the following year." *Source: FAQ — Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**Escalation provision — expulsion order:** FACT: "In the case of a shipping company that has failed to comply with the surrender obligations for two or more consecutive reporting periods, and where other enforcement measures have failed to ensure compliance, the competent authority of the Member State of the port of entry may… issue an expulsion order… every Member State, with the exception of the Member State whose flag the ship is flying, shall refuse entry of the ships under the responsibility of the shipping company concerned into any of its ports until the shipping company fulfils its surrender obligations." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(23)(d) inserting Article 16(11a) into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Operational implication: For cargo verticals requiring time-critical delivery (live events equipment, humanitarian supplies), a carrier subject to an expulsion order could result in cargo being stranded. The workspace should confirm, for high-value or time-sensitive ocean shipments, that carriers have active ETS compliance accounts and no outstanding enforcement actions.

## E. Cap Trajectory — ETS1 (Article 9 amendments)

FACT: The directive amends Article 9 of Directive 2003/87/EC as follows: "In 2024, the Union-wide quantity of allowances shall be decreased by 90 million allowances. In 2026, the Union-wide quantity of allowances shall be decreased by 27 million allowances. In 2024, the Union-wide quantity of allowances shall be increased by 78,4 million allowances for maritime transport. The linear factor shall be 4,3 % from 2024 to 2027 and 4,4 % from 2028." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(11) inserting paragraphs into Article 9 of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The Commission confirmed the 2024 cap: "The Commission informed that the EU ETS cap for 2024 amounts to 1,386,051,745 allowances." *Source: EU ETS Emissions Cap page, European Commission Climate Action, undated (current). https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/carbon-markets/eu-emissions-trading-system-eu-ets/eu-ets-emissions-cap_en.

FACT: *Industry interpretation:* ICAP confirms the 2026 cap: "the cap in 2026 is determined to be 1,185 MtCO₂e" for installations. *Source: EU ETS factsheet, ICAP, 2025/2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/eu-emissions-trading-system-eu-ets.

Operational implication: A tighter cap means higher allowance scarcity and directionally higher ETS prices over time, increasing the cost pass-through to shippers across all transport modes.

## F. CBAM Free Allocation Phase-Out Schedule

FACT: The full CBAM factor schedule as enacted is: "100 % for the period between the entry into force of that Regulation and the end of 2025; 97,5 % in 2026; 95 % in 2027; 90 % in 2028; 77,5 % in 2029; 51,5 % in 2030; 39 % in 2031; 26,5 % in 2032; 14 % in 2033. From 2034, no CBAM factor shall apply." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1a) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification on calculation basis:** FACT: "The reduction of free allocation shall be calculated annually as the average share of the demand for free allocation for the production of goods listed in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2023/956 compared to the calculated total free allocation demand for all installations, for the relevant period referred to in Article 11(1) of this Directive." The reduction is calculated on a sector-average, annual basis, not per individual installation's output. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1a) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

## G. Free Allocation Conditionality (Article 10a — Energy Audit Requirement)

FACT: The directive inserts the following conditionality into free allocation for stationary installations: "If an installation is covered by the obligation to conduct an energy audit or to implement a certified energy management system under Article 8 of Directive 2012/27/EU… and if the recommendations of the audit report or of the certified energy management system are not implemented, unless the pay-back time for the relevant investments exceeds three years or unless the costs of those investments are disproportionate, then the amount of free allocation shall be reduced by 20 %." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1) as amended in Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification:** FACT: "The amount of free allocation shall not be reduced if an operator demonstrates that it has implemented other measures which lead to greenhouse gas emission reductions equivalent to those recommended by the audit report or by the certified energy management system for the installation concerned." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1) as amended, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Operational implication: For clients operating EU manufacturing facilities in CBAM-relevant sectors, failure to implement energy audit recommendations triggers a 20% free allocation reduction. This increases their ETS cost burden, which can feed through to input material costs for automotive or other manufactured goods the workspace ships.

## H. ETS2 — Buildings, Road Transport, and Additional Sectors

**Scope:** FACT: Annex III (inserted by the directive) covers "Release for consumption of fuels which are used for combustion in the buildings, road transport and additional sectors." The exclusions are explicit: "(a) the release for consumption of fuels used in the activities listed in Annex I [ETS1 activities]… (b) the release for consumption of fuels for which the emission factor is zero; (c) the release for consumption of hazardous or municipal waste used as fuel." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Annex (3) inserting Annex III into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Compliance start:** FACT: Article 30e(2) states "From 1 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, by 31 May each year, the regulated entity surrenders an amount of allowances covered by this Chapter that is equal to the regulated entity's total emissions." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30e(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng. (Note: ICAP confirms start was postponed to 2028 by March 2026 Council/Parliament decision.)

**Linear reduction factor:** FACT: "the linear reduction factor should be set at 5,10 %" for 2024–2027 trajectory. From 2028, "the linear reduction factor of 5,38 %." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, recital (80), EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Price ceiling mechanism:** FACT: "Where the average price of allowances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article exceeds a price of EUR 45 for a period of two consecutive months, 20 million allowances covered by this Chapter shall be released from the market stability reserve in accordance with Article 1a(7) of Decision (EU) 2015/1814. Indexation based on the European index of consumer prices for 2020 shall apply. Allowances shall be released through the mechanism provided for in this paragraph up to 31 December 2029." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30h(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Postponement trigger:** FACT: The directive provides that if "the average TTF gas price for the six calendar months ending 30 June 2026 was higher than the average TTF gas price in February and March 2022" OR "the average Brent crude oil price for the six calendar months ending 30 June 2026 was more than twice the average Brent crude oil price during the five preceding years," the system is delayed by one year (to 2028 in the original text; effectively further delayed now that March 2026 postponement has already been enacted). *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30k(1) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**ETS2 penalty:** FACT (ICAP): "Covered entities must pay an excess emissions penalty of EUR 100 (USD 113), adjusted for inflation with 2013 as the base year, for each tCO₂ emitted for which no allowance has been surrendered." *Source: EU ETS 2 factsheet, ICAP, 2025/2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/eu-emissions-trading-system-buildings-and-road-transport-eu-ets-2.

## Outermost Region Exemption

FACT: "An obligation to surrender allowances shall not arise in respect of emissions released until 31 December 2030 from voyages between a port located in an outermost region of a Member State and a port located in the same Member State, including voyages between ports within an outermost region and voyages between ports in the outermost regions of the same Member State, and from the activities, within a port, of such ships in relation to such voyages." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 12(3-b) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Scope of this exemption:** The Canary Islands, Madeira, Azores, Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana, Réunion, Mayotte, and Saint-Martin qualify as outermost regions. Voyages between these ports and mainland ports of the same Member State (e.g., Lanzarote–Valencia, Guadeloupe–Marseille) are exempt from ETS through 2030. Voyages from these regions to another EU Member State's ports are not exempt on this basis.

## Small Island Exemption

FACT: Article 12(3-d) allows Member States to request that emissions from passenger ships and ro-pax ships between "a port of an island under the jurisdiction of that requesting Member State, with no road or rail link with the mainland and with a population of fewer than 200 000 permanent residents" be exempted from surrender obligations "until 31 December 2030." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 12(3-d) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification:** This exemption applies only to "passenger ships, other than cruise passenger ships, and by ro-pax ships" on these specific routes. General cargo vessels are not covered by this derogation.

## ETS2 — National Carbon Tax Derogation

FACT: Article 30e(3) provides that "until 31 December 2030, by way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2… where a regulated entity established in a given Member State is subject to a national carbon tax in force for the years 2027 to 2030, covering the activity referred to in Annex III, the competent authority of the Member State concerned may exempt that regulated entity from the obligation to surrender allowances… provided that: (a) the Member State concerned notifies the Commission of that national carbon tax by 31 December 2023, and the national law setting the tax rates applicable for the years 2027 to 2030 has, by that date, entered into force; (b) for the reference year, the national carbon tax of the Member State concerned effectively paid by that regulated entity is higher than the average auction clearing price of the emissions trading system established under this Chapter." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30e(3) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Analytical inference: In Member States with pre-existing carbon taxes on road fuel (e.g., Austria, Germany, which had national carbon pricing systems), regulated entities may be exempt from ETS2 surrender obligations if the national tax is higher than the ETS2 clearing price. This creates a complex multi-jurisdiction cost environment for cross-border European road freight. The workspace should confirm with European road freight partners which regulatory regime applies in each Member State where fuel is released for consumption.

## European Commission FAQ on Maritime ETS

The European Commission has published an FAQ document on maritime transport in the EU ETS (updated 02/04/2025). Key operational provisions synthesized below:

**Surrender timing:** FACT: "Shipping companies must surrender (use) their first ETS allowances by 30 September 2025 for emissions reported in 2024." The schedule is: "2025: 40% of emissions reported for 2024 must be covered by emission allowances; 2026: 70% of emissions reported for 2025; 2027 and beyond: 100% of reported emissions." *Source: FAQ — Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**Port of call definition for voyage calculation:** FACT: The FAQ confirms that "stops of containerships in the neighbouring container transhipment ports listed in the corresponding implementing act" are excluded from the definition of port of call. *Source: FAQ — Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**Carbon credits:** FACT: "Carbon credits or certificates cannot be used for EU ETS compliance purposes." *Source: FAQ — Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**Cross-year voyages:** FACT: "For voyages starting and ending in two different calendar years, the respective data must be accounted under each reporting period." *Source: FAQ — Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**EEA applicability:** FACT: "The MRV Maritime Regulation and ETS Directive apply to Norway and Iceland. The texts have been incorporated into the EEA Agreement (Annex XX)." *Source: FAQ — Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

## BIMCO Contractual Guidance

Industry interpretation (BIMCO, shipping industry association): BIMCO has published clause frameworks addressing how shipping companies and charterers allocate ETS costs: "ETS – Emission Trading Scheme Allowances Clause for Time Charter Parties 2022," "ETS – Emission Scheme Freight Clause for Voyage Charter Parties 2023," and related instruments. BIMCO notes that "if the parties have not agreed to include an ETS clause in an existing contract, then one party cannot force the other to do so." *Source: BIMCO EU ETS page, BIMCO, undated (current). https://www.bimco.org/news-insights/trending-topics/eu-ets/.

This is labeled as industry operator interpretation and is cited for navigation only, not as legal authority. The workspace, when negotiating ocean freight contracts with carriers on European trade lanes, should confirm whether applicable ETS cost clauses are present.
